subject: Capacity bridging & ROI case for upgrade — Q2 usage review
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara@greenstreet.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@greenstreet.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q2 usage spike & options for term extension

Hi Tessa / Vivek,

Hope you’re both well. We just closed out Q2 and saw a meaningful spike in token consumption tied to a new realtime feature we launched mid-June. I’ve attached our Q2 usage export — spikes are concentrated on the conversational endpoint and a 30% increase in peak RPS.

We’re approaching the end of our current 12-month term and are re-evaluating capacity / pricing for the next year. Two asks:

- Can Redwood provide a short ROI breakdown comparing our current committed tier vs a 20–30% capacity bump (run-rate + unit economics)?
- What flexibility is there for a short-term bridging top-up (1–3 months) while we finalize product forecasts?

We’re also starting procurement, so a redlined amendment would be helpful. Monica — looping in contracts for any doc questions.

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Director of Applied AI, GreenStreet Labs
attachments: GreenStreet_Q2_usage_report.pdf
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara@greenstreet.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jul 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Q2 usage spike & options for term extension

Sara — thanks for the usage file, that was helpful. Quick read-through here and a short recap of what I’m seeing:

- Peak tokens (conversational) are driving 62% of incremental spend; peak RPS increases latency risk under current pooling.
- Your average per-request token mix has shifted +18% on completion tokens (longer replies), which increases per-token cost.
- There’s a clear case for short-term prefix caching on high-frequency prompts which should reduce incremental spend by ~8–10% immediately.

Proposal (high level):
- Short-term bridging: 2-month top-up of +25% committed capacity (applied as burst credits) to avoid throttling while you stabilize usage patterns.
- Term option: 12 -> 18 month renewal with an option to re-evaluate after 9 months; price tiers adjusted for higher token mix.
- Tech mitigations: enable prefix caching + increase hot KV cache to reduce peak tail latency.

I’ve attached a proposed amendment with a pricing sketch and a capacity pricing breakdown. If this looks reasonable I can get a formal redline and an ROI sketch from finance. Monica, can you confirm proposed SLAs for a 25% bump and whether we can offer accelerated billing terms?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: GSL_proposed_amendment_2028-07.docx; capacity_pricing_breakdown.xlsx

Naomi / Tessa — quick internal on GreenStreet: they’re strategic (AI infra reference), and the 25% top-up for 2 months is reasonable to avoid churn on the product team side. A couple of asks from finance/sales:

- Can we give a one-time 12% list discount on the incremental capacity if they sign the 18-month term? We want to make the ask attractive without setting a precedent for future short-term top-ups.
- SLA uplift (99.9 -> 99.95) for the bumped cohort — can we absorb the marginal cost for a single quarter?

Naomi — can you advise if the 12% concession is OK and if we can handle billing as an upfront invoice for the 2-month top-up? I’ll note that we should keep the DocuSign amendment concise and include usage caps for the bridging credits.

Subject: GSL proposal: 2-month bridging top-up + 18m renewal option (ROI & next steps)

Sara — thanks for your patience while we finalized internal approvals. Below is the consolidated offer and a short ROI recap.

Offer summary:
- 2-month bridging top-up: +25% committed capacity as burst credits, billed upfront.
- Renewal term: 18 months starting after the bridge window.
- Pricing: 12% one-time concession on incremental capacity if they sign the 18-month renewal by Aug 8, 2028.
- SLA: temporary uplift to 99.95% for the 2-month bridge; permanent SLA remains at your contracted level unless otherwise amended.
- Tech: we’ll enable prefix caching and increase your hot KV allocation immediately (expected 8–10% cost reduction within 10 days).

ROI snapshot (high level):
- Avoided downtime / throttling risk: estimated retention value of $120k in ARR over next 12 months if product experiments continue without interruption.
- Incremental bridge cost (net of discount): ~$38k; expected efficiency gains reduce net impact to ~$28k over 2 months.
- Net benefit: positive if even one product rollout avoids delay — qualitative upside plus predictable unit economics.

Attachments: GSL_proposed_amendment_2028-07.docx, capacity_pricing_breakdown.xlsx, GreenStreet_Q2_usage_report.pdf

Next steps:
1) If this is acceptable, sign the attached amendment (DocuSign link below) by Aug 8 to lock the concession.
2) Monica will kick off a short tech onboarding for caching and KV tuning (2-week window).
3) Finance will issue an upfront invoice for the bridge; Naomi, will confirm invoicing cadence.
